**Decisions.** I adopted your four recommendations. One addition to rule 2: origins whose kind is Unknown still count, because the child's audit found they come only from runtime values.

**Results on the frozen final binary**, counting repeats of one bad value as one group:

| Repository | Tier | Groups | Runtime-confirmed | False positives |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Feathr | Proven | 14 (34 sites) | 8 | 1 |
| xlwings | Conditional | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| Seaborn | Conditional | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| mutagen | both | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Dramatiq | both | 0 | 0 | 0 |

- **Demonstration bugs.** xlwings `_xlmac.py:706` and Seaborn `distributions.py:947` are now reported as Conditional findings. Both are runtime-confirmed.
- **Feathr false positive.** It is the lines 209 to 215 group, already known to be unreachable in practice.
- **Other fixes.** The corpus harness reports no failures. The Mesa fix is partial and is described under open work.

**What qualification caught.** The first frozen run failed two acceptance checks. Every cause was an analyzer bug, and each is fixed at its source:
- **Feathr.** Feathr lost all 34 Proven findings. A wildcard import made `abc.ABC` look unresolved, so the dispatch fix treated its subclasses as intercepted.
- **xlwings.** 22 of 31 Conditional findings were false positives. A constructor called through a module path (`xw.Book(...)`) returned `__init__`'s `None`. A keyword argument also defined the class of `**kwargs`.
- **mutagen.** All 25 Conditional findings were false positives. The same constructor bug affected `mutagen.id3.ID3(...)` after two imports of the same package.
- **Duplicate tier rows.** The Conditional policy still reported sites that another caller context proves. The tier filter now runs after rows from all contexts merge.

**Also landed.**
- **#3759 closed.** Repeats of one bad value on the same path now collapse into the first finding, with the later sites listed on it.
- **Mesa (#3331), partial.** Read-only `__dict__` calls no longer count as writes. A write whose receiver has a known bound now affects only that bound.

**Still open.**
- **Mesa is still missed.** 17 dynamic writes with unbounded receivers remain, for example the dynamically created GridCell class at `grid.py:54`.
- **Package scans cap out.** At the unchanged 180-second cap, the package policies for xlwings (Conditional), Seaborn, mutagen, Odysseus and Glom do not finish. I did not count them as clean. The mutagen and xlwings results above come from complete per-file queries.
- **Comparison with ty.** The five blind repositories need complete scans first.
- **Go test.** `the_diff_base_activates_exact_curated_go_packs` failed twice on plain master but passed in later runs, so it is likely flaky. No issue tracks it.

What landed is the epic's main demonstration. xlwings and Seaborn are now detected, ty misses both, and there is 1 false positive in 18 finding groups across the controls.

I recommend keeping the epic open until Mesa is detected and the blind-repository comparison runs on complete scans.
what is the path to landing those?
I'll check the current state of the completion tickets before answering, since another agent has owned them since mid-September.

There are three separate paths. Completion comes first, because the ty comparison depends on it. Mesa is independent and can run in parallel.

**1. Completion (#3334, #3163).** Both tickets have stalled. The last real progress was on 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-19. #3334 still carries an `agent-in-progress` label but has no assignee.
- **Old evidence.** On #3334, generator comprehensions in one Odysseus file exhaust the flow-evaluation budget. On #3163, a single large procedure exhausts the per-root nested-entries budget. Both measurements predate Design 1, Design 2 and today's fixes.
- **Currently capped.** The xlwings Conditional policy, Seaborn, mutagen, Odysseus and Glom do not finish in 180 seconds. xlwings is close, at about 172 to 178 CPU seconds. mutagen is far over: its 57 per-file queries took about 1,000 seconds in total.
- **Path.** Profile each capped run on the current frozen binary, find the dominant cost, and make that work cheaper. Raising budgets is not allowed.
- **Unknown.** Whether one cause dominates or each repository has its own.

**2. Mesa (#3331).** Seventeen dynamic writes still suppress the finding. The replay records why each write's receiver could not be bounded:

| Why the receiver is unbounded | Write sites |
| --- | --- |
| Receiver survey truncated | 8 |
| Unmodeled load | 4 |
| Field slot incomplete | 2 |
| Dynamically created class (`grid.py:54`) | 1 |
| Annotation upper bound only | 1 |
| Uncertain flow | 1 |

There are three possible levers. How many sites each would clear is unknown:
- **Survey truncation.** Making the receiver survey finish within its limit would cover the largest group. This overlaps with the completion work.
- **Write key.** A write can install `_agent_to_index` only if its attribute name can be that string. Writes with a constant name, or a dictionary with known keys, could be excluded.
- **Dynamic class creation.** A class built with `type(name, (GridCell,), ...)` still subclasses GridCell, so writes to its instances can be bounded by GridCell.

The first step is a census of the 17 sites, recording which lever applies to each one. I recommend against treating unbounded dynamic writes as just another remainder in the Conditional tier. That is how ty finds Mesa, and it is likely the source of much of ty's noise.

**3. The ty comparison.** This needs three things:
- **Complete scans.** In the 2026-09-13 blind pass (#3335), only 1 of the 5 repositories completed. That was on a much older binary.
- **A predeclared protocol.** It should state the repositories, how diagnostics are sampled from each tool, and runtime triage of a fixed sample from both tools. A ty baseline already exists: 49 false positives in 50 sampled diagnostics.
- **Recall.** The #3335 pass found no new bugs. The comparison only supports the epic's claim if Bifrost finds real bugs on repositories it was not tuned on. That risk is real.

**Recommended first step.** Rerun the five blind repositories and the capped controls with the current frozen binary. This needs no build and takes about an hour. It shows how big the completion problem is today and gives fresh profiles for #3334.

I've cleaned up and paused, with nothing left running.

**Disk.**
- **Freed about 160 GB.** `/home` now has 574 GB free, up from 505 GB. `/` has 314 GB free, up from 222 GB.
- **`mbx clean` found nothing.** None of my children's worktrees had an mbx-managed target, because they built through the repository's isolated-target script with explicit target directories, or on EC2.
- **Deleted targets.** I removed those explicit targets instead: two persistent ones in the hunt directory, the combined-gate target in `/tmp`, and two leftover isolated targets in `/tmp`. The source paths inside them confirmed they came from my children's worktrees. I left older isolated targets in `/tmp` alone, because they belong to other sessions.
- **Worktrees.** All of my children's worktrees are removed.

**EC2.** I terminated the instance and cancelled its spot request, and I confirmed nothing remains running or pending. I kept the security group and key pair, so `bifrost5-python-hunt/ec2/relaunch.sh` can start a new box.

**Lost work.** Suspending the session stopped the experiment child before it handed back. It had confirmed that Mesa line 140 becomes a Conditional finding when both relaxations are on. It had not finished measuring what else they add across the corpus. I saved its two commits as patches, plus 13 MB of partial results, in `bifrost5-python-hunt/handoff/unbounded-write-experiment-2026-10-01/`.

**Where things stand.**
- **Landed on master.** Three changes landed this session:
  - The blob-hashing fix cut Glom's CPU time by 27 percent.
  - The Mesa precision stack cut the writes blocking line 140 from 17 to 5. All corpus controls are unchanged.
  - The comparison protocol and its reference-machine amendment are recorded in the plan.
- **Waiting on your decision:**
  - **Mesa.** Should the Conditional tier treat writes with an unknown receiver and an unknown name as a stated condition? Should it accept an annotation as an origin when the class has no workspace subclasses? Mesa needs both.
  - **Completion.** Fitting the 180-second cap likely needs callee summaries parameterized by entry context. That is a redesign of the dataflow engine.
- **Blocked.** The comparison with ty waits on completion, because none of the five blind repositories finishes within the cap.

The `agent-in-progress` claims on #3745, #3331, #3334 and #3163 are still in place, since this is a pause. I can release them if you'd prefer.
